title: AVO sub-final (Romaric)
description: Sub-final exam covering PCB fundamentals, Bourdon tube sensing, flight director command bars, microphones, splice bonding checks, AC frequency/RL circuits, battery series/parallel wiring, AFCS go-around and autothrottle indications, filters, digital codes, and TCAS jitter.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of a PCB?
options: It does not need point-to-point wiring
It needs special training to repair
questions.explanation: Because components and traces are densely packed and soldered directly onto the board, properly tracing faults and reworking a PCB requires specially trained technicians and equipment, unlike simpler point-to-point wiring.

questions.question: A Bourdon tube is used to measure which of the following? (1 = pressure, 2 = temperature, 3 = position, 4 = quantity)
questions.explanation: A Bourdon tube directly measures pressure by straightening under internal pressure, and this same principle is also used in filled-system (Bourdon-tube) thermometers, where a temperature-sensing bulb generates a pressure that the tube then converts into a temperature reading.

questions.question: If the heading display is 10° and a right-turn command is required, where will the command bar move?
questions.explanation: The heading error signal commands a turn in the required direction, so with a right turn needed to reach the selected heading, the command bar deflects to the right.

questions.question: Which type of microphone uses a capacitor?
questions.explanation: An electrostatic (condenser) microphone forms a capacitor between a thin conductive diaphragm and a fixed backplate; sound waves vary the spacing between them, changing the capacitance and producing the audio signal.

questions.question: Which tool is used to check the bonding of a splice?
questions.explanation: A digital multimeter is used to check the low-resistance bonding continuity across a splice, confirming the joint provides a solid, low-resistance electrical connection.

questions.question: What is the output frequency if a 50 Hz frequency is doubled?
questions.explanation: Doubling a 50 Hz signal simply multiplies its frequency by two, giving 100 Hz.

questions.question: If two 12 V batteries are connected in series, what is the total voltage?
questions.explanation: In a series connection, the individual cell/battery voltages add together, so two 12 V batteries in series give 24 V total, while the amp-hour (Ah) capacity stays the same as a single battery.

questions.question: If two 12 V batteries are connected in parallel, what is the total voltage?
questions.explanation: In a parallel connection, the voltage stays the same as a single battery (12 V), while the combined amp-hour (Ah) capacity increases, since the batteries share the load current between them.

questions.question: To engage the go-around mode, you press the:
questions.explanation: The TO/GA (take-off/go-around) switch, mounted on the thrust levers, commands go-around mode, forcing the flight director to a pitch-up, wings-level command.

questions.question: Which control input automatically activates the flight director during a go-around?
options: GA selection on the TO/GA switch
questions.explanation: Pressing the go-around switch forces the mode selector to the GA position, which automatically brings the flight director command bars into view, commanding a pitch-up and wings-level attitude.

questions.question: Autothrottle activation is indicated on:
questions.explanation: Autothrottle mode status appears in the flight mode annunciator (FMA) strip on the PFD/EADI, alongside the pitch and roll mode annunciations.

questions.question: In an RL circuit, if the frequency doubles, the current will:
questions.explanation: Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL increases as frequency increases, which increases the circuit's total impedance and therefore decreases the current for a fixed applied voltage.

questions.question: What is the opposite of a band-reject filter?
questions.explanation: A band-reject (notch/stop) filter blocks a specific range of frequencies while passing everything else, which is the exact opposite of a band-pass filter, which passes only a specific range of frequencies and blocks everything else.

questions.question: What can be done to increase the current in an RL circuit?
questions.explanation: Since inductive reactance XL = 2πfL decreases as frequency decreases, lowering the frequency reduces the circuit's total impedance, which increases the current for a fixed applied voltage.

questions.question: Which 6-bit alphanumeric code can represent 64 characters?
questions.explanation: BCDIC is a 6-bit code, giving 2^6 = 64 possible characters, unlike the 8-bit EBCDIC or the (originally) 7-bit ASCII, both of which can represent a larger character set.

questions.question: What is the formula for capacitors connected in series?
questions.explanation: Capacitors in series combine like resistors in parallel: the reciprocal of the total capacitance equals the sum of the reciprocals of each individual capacitance, which always makes the total series capacitance smaller than the smallest individual capacitor.

questions.question: What is the second name of an AC alternator?
questions.explanation: An alternator and an AC generator refer to the same machine — a rotating device that generates alternating current — so 'AC generator' is simply the alternative name for an alternator.

questions.question: The deliberate random variation of the time interval between successive interrogations is called:
questions.explanation: Jitter is intentionally introduced into the timing of successive TCAS/DME interrogations so that interrogations from different aircraft do not consistently overlap or synchronize, reducing the chance of repeated mutual interference (garbling) between systems.
